findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5076 is "Fix hostnames on UFs". "TA for Nutanix Prism" is Splunkbase 3103 with app directory `TA-nutanix`, and Prism Central has a separate "TA for Nutanix Prism Central" (8349, `TA-nutanix-PC`). The wrong ID and directory propagate into app, dataSources, implementation, references and every `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/Splunk_TA_nutanix/...` path in detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: Install the add-on as **`Splunk_TA_nutanix`** — **TA for Nutanix Prism** ([Splunkbase 5076](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5076))
findings.suggested_fix: Use TA for Nutanix Prism (3103, TA-nutanix) for Prism Element and TA for Nutanix Prism Central (8349, TA-nutanix-PC) for Prism Central; fix paths and the reference link.

findings.explanation: The text asserts which PC sourcetype is real and which is "non-existent" without any source. The PC alias and the `[nutanix://...]` stanza keys (nutanix_host, verify_server_cert, ca_certs_path) look guessed. The repository guide lists only `nutanix:cluster`.
findings.quote: **`nutanix:prism_central:cluster`** (Prism Central, alias `nutanix:pc:cluster` in some TA builds) ... Do **not** use a non-existent `nutanix:prism_central:clusters` sourcetype.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the cluster sourcetypes and input stanza in the Nutanix Splunk user guides for TA-nutanix and TA-nutanix-PC, then state only documented names.

findings.explanation: The sample EOS table is internally contradictory (newer 6.5.3/6.5.4 patches end support before 6.5.2, AOS 1.0 "EOS 2010") and maps versions to themselves as replacements. Readers who copy it get false EOS_BREACH/EOS_RISK results. The baseline CSV also carries an unused `eos_date` column and `0000-00-00` placeholders.
findings.suggested_fix: Label the rows clearly as placeholders without dates, or populate from the Nutanix EOL list with real dates. Drop the unused eos_date column from the baseline example.

findings.explanation: The SPL is raw-index only with no cimSpl, and periodic cluster-inventory snapshots are not Change events. Declaring CIM Change implies a change-audit mapping the UC does not provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty, or keep only Inventory if you add field aliases/tags that actually populate the Inventory data model.

findings.explanation: In PCI DSS v4.0, requirement 6.2 is bespoke-software development; identifying and risk-ranking vulnerabilities is 6.3.1 (6.1 in v3.2.1). ISO 27001 A.12.6.1 is 2013 numbering (A.8.8 in 2022).
findings.quote: **PCI DSS 6.2** (ensure known vulnerabilities are identified and risk-ranked)
findings.suggested_fix: Check the PCI DSS v4.0.1 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause numbers and cite the version used.

findings.explanation: None of the scenarios applies to a daily version-posture report. The real false positives (OEM-locked AOS builds, NC2 vendor-managed lifecycle, long-form vs short version strings, stale EOS lookup) are buried in the Tune section.
findings.quote: Planned work for 'Nutanix AOS Version Compliance' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `cluster_uuid`, `cluster_name` remains in-scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Move those causes into knownFalsePositives with their mitigation (baseline row per cluster, NC2 exclusion, EOS lookup refresh).

findings.explanation: Microsoft 365 and ServiceNow are not monitored equipment for an AOS version report; ServiceNow is only an alert destination.
The legal hub and the nutanix.dev root are not lifecycle or API references for this UC.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the Nutanix End of Life policy/EOL list, the Prism v2.0 cluster API reference, and the correct Splunkbase TA page.

findings.explanation: Marked verified although the add-on ID is wrong and the saved SPL cannot run as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Set to draft until the corrected SPL runs against real TA-nutanix data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search begins with five `//` lines. SPL has no `//` comment syntax, so these become search terms, and the backtick-quoted `nutanix:cluster` and `nutanix_aos_baseline.csv` inside them are parsed as macro calls, so the search errors or matches nothing. Use ``` ... ``` inline comments or a `comment` macro.
`lts_breach` tests `is_lts=0`, but the Prism JSON value extracted by spath is the boolean string true/false, so LTS_BREACH never fires.

The header comment promises in-flight suppression only "for <2h", but the where clause drops any row whose target_version differs from the running NOS, with no time bound. A stalled upgrade is silently suppressed forever.
`sort 0 - severity_bucket` sorts strings descending (warning > info > critical), so critical rows land below warnings, contrary to the intent.

summary: The baseline-versus-running design is sound and well explained, but the UC names the wrong add-on (Splunkbase 5076 is unrelated; there is no Splunk_TA_nutanix). The saved SPL also opens with `//` comment lines that Splunk does not support, and several logic branches (LTS breach, in-flight suppression, severity sort) do not do what the prose claims.
